definitions.gloss: small shrine, wayside shrine, miniature shrine
definitions.explanation: A small, simple shrine typically found at roadsides, in forests, or at the base of trees or rocks. Much smaller than a formal shrine building, often housing a local deity or spirit.

examples.japanese: {道端|みちばた}に{小|ちい}さな{祠|ほこら}がある。
examples.english: There is a small shrine by the roadside.

examples.japanese: {山道|やまみち}の{途中|とちゅう}で{古|ふる}い{祠|ほこら}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found an old wayside shrine partway along the mountain trail.

examples.japanese: {村|むら}の{人|ひと}たちは、{大木|たいぼく}の{根元|ねもと}にある{祠|ほこら}に{毎朝|まいあさ}{花|はな}を{供|そな}えている。
examples.english: The villagers offer flowers every morning at the small shrine at the base of the large tree.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Found throughout Japan at roadsides, mountain paths, and in neighborhoods. These miniature shrines enshrine local kami (deities) or spirits and are maintained by the local community. They are much smaller and simpler than formal {神社|じんじゃ} (Shinto shrines), sometimes no bigger than a birdhouse.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {神社|じんじゃ}: a formal Shinto shrine with buildings and grounds
- {社|やしろ}: a shrine (somewhat literary)
- {地蔵|じぞう}: a Buddhist roadside statue (different tradition but similar wayside placement)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小|ちい}さな{祠|ほこら}: a small shrine
- {道端|みちばた}の{祠|ほこら}: a roadside shrine
- {祠|ほこら}に{手|て}を{合|あ}わせる: to pray at a small shrine
- {祠|ほこら}を{祀|まつ}る: to enshrine a deity in a small shrine
